item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Sunday, October 11, 2026
item.description: Today: Shane Gillis’s third SNL brings a live F-bomb and a monologue that split the internet; Blade Runner 2099 trailer: Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh hunt for missing replicants; Ella Langley cancels a sold-out Tulsa show over a threat police say wasn’t credible; Kelly Clarkson says a Brooklyn shop gave her the Pretty Woman treatment: “You’re an idiot”.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday’s conversation: Shane Gillis’s third SNL hosting gig brings an uncensored F-bomb and a monologue people can’t stop arguing about, Prime Video shows off Blade Runner 2099 at Comic Con, Ella Langley cancels a sold-out Tulsa show over a threat police say wasn’t credible, and Kelly Clarkson calls out a Brooklyn shop for giving her the Pretty Woman treatment.

Shane Gillis’s third SNL brings a live F-bomb and a monologue that split the internet

TV

Gillis was cut from SNL’s cast in 2019, days after he was announced, over resurfaced videos of him mocking Asian accents and using slurs. Saturday was his third time hosting. His monologue included a joke that gaining weight made him “look like a lesbian” and a bit about women who dress like “whores” at the gym. Variety says it also had strong defenders online, and the fight broke down largely along political lines.

Then, in a Dr. Seuss “Green Eggs and Ham” sketch, he let an F-bomb slip. The censors missed it on the live broadcast, Mikey Day called it out in character, and Gillis said “sorry about earlier” at goodnights. Deadline says new cast member Grace Reiter saved an otherwise dull episode. Rosalía won raves for singing “Reliquia” en pointe and “Magnolias” under an in-studio rainstorm. The show is off until Halloween, when Inde Navarrette hosts with Gracie Abrams.

  • Read at Deadline
  • Read at Variety
  • Read at LateNighter

Blade Runner 2099 trailer: Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh hunt for missing replicants

Streaming

Prime Video premiered a new trailer and key art at New York Comic Con on Saturday. The eight-episode limited series is set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049, in a Los Angeles now run by replicants. Schafer plays Cora, a fugitive who takes on one last identity as a Blade Runner, and Yeoh plays Olwen, a replicant with only days to live. Their case starts with 38 replicants who have gone missing over the past year.

Showrunner Silka Luisa has called it “Chinatown set in the world of Blade Runner,” and Ridley Scott is an executive producer. All eight episodes drop Nov. 25, and Luisa says the season is “a complete story within itself.”

  • Trailer on YouTube
  • Read at Deadline
  • Read at Polygon

Ella Langley cancels a sold-out Tulsa show over a threat police say wasn’t credible

Music

About two hours before Friday’s show at Tulsa’s 19,000-seat BOK Center, a caller warned of “great harm” with “shots fired and bombs.” Police searched the arena twice with bomb dogs and found no credible threat. Capt. Richard Meulenberg said police never told Langley’s team to cancel, and they suspect swatting. ABC News reports the FBI is helping with the investigation.

“I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way,” Langley wrote, adding that refund details are coming. It’s a rattling moment for one of country’s hottest stars: in September her “Choosin’ Texas” became the longest-running No. 1 in Hot 100 history. Her Dandelion Tour runs through Oct. 31.

  • Listen on Spotify
  • Read at BBC
  • Read at ABC News

Kelly Clarkson says a Brooklyn shop gave her the Pretty Woman treatment: “You’re an idiot”

Celebrity

Clarkson posted on X Saturday that she drove to Art of Play, a Brooklyn shop that sells magic, puzzles and games, and an employee looked at her “as if I couldn’t afford it” and offered to find “something comparable.” “Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” she wrote, telling followers to go there “if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman.”

Fans hit the store with one-star Google reviews. Art of Play declined to comment to Page Six, but it appeared to respond on Instagram by sharing a customer review praising its staff’s kindness. Us Weekly reports that post was later deleted.

  • Read at Complex
  • Read at AOL

Bottom of the news

  • Usher and Chris Brown cancel four R&B Tour stadium dates ahead of Brown’s Oct. 26 sentencing in London; the tour picks back up Nov. 5 in Atlanta.
  • On HBO’s Jay-Z in 8, Jay-Z answers Kanye’s old “Big Brother” complaint about Coldplay: “We don’t own people.”
  • Kid Rock draws backlash after opening for Trump at a Tennessee rally and sitting down with Lara Trump on Fox News.
  • Eminem releases “MADARA,” a Naruto-inspired track with EZ Mil, Hideyoshi and Madara voice actor Neil Kaplan.
  • Matthew Lillard’s NYCC answer embracing Scream’s Billy and Stu as queer icons goes viral.
  • Olivia Culpo gives birth to her second baby with Christian McCaffrey.

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Saturday, October 10, 2026
item.description: Today: Mike Flanagan’s The Exorcist: Martyrs trailer is here, with Scarlett Johansson hunting a killer; Other Mommy shrugs off brutal reviews for a No. 1 opening, while The Social Reckoning fizzles; Britney Spears releases “She’ll Never Be Me,” a lost 2001 song she co-wrote with Justin Timberlake; Unsealed texts show Ryan Reynolds calling Justin Baldoni a “predator and sociopath”.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday’s conversation: Mike Flanagan’s Exorcist reboot drops its first trailer, Jessica Chastain’s badly reviewed Other Mommy scares up a No. 1 opening while Aaron Sorkin’s Social Network follow-up stalls, Britney Spears releases a lost song she wrote with Justin Timberlake, and newly unsealed texts show Ryan Reynolds unloading on Justin Baldoni.

Mike Flanagan’s The Exorcist: Martyrs trailer is here, with Scarlett Johansson hunting a killer

Movies

Flanagan unveiled the first trailer at Blumhouse’s New York Comic Con panel Friday night. Johansson plays Detective Julie Miller, who put away a serial killer called Father Sunday (John Leguizamo) and sees him executed, only to find her name written in blood at a murder scene 13 years later. Laurence Fishburne, Diane Lane, Sasha Calle and Jacobi Jupe co-star.

Flanagan told the crowd it’s the scariest movie he’s ever made and “unlike any other Exorcist movie,” citing The Exorcist III and William Peter Blatty’s Legion as influences. It isn’t a sequel to 2023’s Believer. It opens in theaters March 12, 2027.

  • Trailer on YouTube
  • Read at USA Today
  • Read at The Hindu

Other Mommy shrugs off brutal reviews for a No. 1 opening, while The Social Reckoning fizzles

Box Office

Jessica Chastain’s Universal–Blumhouse horror movie, where she plays both a mom and the doppelgänger stalking her daughter, made $12.3 million Friday (including $3.6 million in Thursday previews) and is tracking toward about $27.5 million for the weekend. That’s a win for a film that cost under $20 million, even with some critics calling it Chastain’s worst movie.

Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning, with Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg, Mikey Madison as the Facebook whistleblower and Jeremy Allen White as the reporter, is looking at roughly $6 million. The Social Network opened to $22 million 16 years ago.

  • Other Mommy trailer on YouTube
  • Read at Deadline
  • Read at Gold Derby

Britney Spears releases “She’ll Never Be Me,” a lost 2001 song she co-wrote with Justin Timberlake

Music

The track was recorded for her self-titled 2001 album, when she and Timberlake were dating, and fans have only had low-quality leaks until now. It’s the first of five unreleased songs on a 25th-anniversary edition of Britney due Nov. 6, and her team says “more surprises are coming every week.”

It’s also her first new release since “Mind Your Business” with will.i.am in 2023. Spears hasn’t commented, but fans online are calling it single-worthy.

  • Listen on Spotify
  • Read at USA Today
  • Read at RTÉ

Unsealed texts show Ryan Reynolds calling Justin Baldoni a “predator and sociopath”

Celebrity

Court documents from Blake Lively’s legal fight with Baldoni, obtained by Page Six, include 2024 texts from Reynolds to author Colleen Hoover and to his agent during the It Ends With Us press tour. He calls Baldoni a “human rounding error” and blasts Sony for not publicly defending his wife sooner.

Lively and the remaining defendants settled in May, but the texts have reopened the whole saga online. A source close to Reynolds says he was protecting his wife from a crisis PR campaign.

  • Read at Page Six

Bottom of the news

  • Shane Gillis hosts SNL for the third time tonight, with Rosalía as musical guest.
  • Pretty Little Liars star Keegan Allen was reportedly attacked by masked assailants in Los Angeles.
  • Meghan Markle has tea with Malala Yousafzai at Claridge’s in her first public outing since moving back to the U.K.
  • Catherine Zeta-Jones jokes she has “no intention” of reading Michael Douglas’s tell-all memoir, then says she will.
  • Marvel’s VisionQuest buzz builds after its NYCC first-episode screening, ahead of the Oct. 14 Disney+ premiere.
  • Disney+’s Remarried Empress debuts at the Busan International Film Festival.

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Friday, October 9, 2026
item.description:
Friday · October 9, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Friday’s conversation: Ben Affleck’s Animals lands on Netflix to some of the worst reviews of his directing career, Troye Sivan drops his fourth album, Taylor Swift books an Oscar-season stage at the Academy Museum Gala, and Crazy Rich Asians is coming back as an HBO series with its original stars.
Movies

Ben Affleck’s Animals hits Netflix, and critics are not kind

Affleck directs, co-writes and stars as Mark Kimball, a long-shot Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped days before the election. Kerry Washington plays his wife Abigail, Gillian Anderson is the ransom specialist who tells them whatever secrets they’ve kept need to come out now, and Steven Yeun is his campaign manager. It’s streaming now on Netflix and playing in select theaters.

Reviews are rough. RogerEbert.com calls it “easily Affleck’s worst directorial effort,” the AP gives it two stars out of four, and Deadline says it’s “stretched too thin.” Several critics point out how closely the setup follows Kurosawa’s High and Low, which Spike Lee just remade as Highest 2 Lowest, without crediting it. Variety’s Guy Lodge is kinder, calling it “nasty” and “compulsive.”

Trailer →   ·   RogerEbert.com review →   ·   Variety review →

Music

Troye Sivan releases She’s the Best, a looser, late-night follow-up to Something to Give Each Other

The 12-track album is out today on Interscope, with Nicole Kidman starring in the title-track video, a Madonna “Music” interpolation on “Party,” Charli XCX on backing vocals and Lily-Rose Depp on the closer, “Lost Time.” Jack Antonoff and the 1975’s George Daniel are among the collaborators. Sivan has said he wanted it to feel a little “sloppy” compared with his 2023 dance-pop record.

Critics mostly like it: Clash gives it 8/10, NME calls it a “pleasantly confounding” trip through ’90s alt-dance, and it’s averaging 80 on Album of the Year. The video for “FF,” which Sivan calls the gayest of his career, is driving most of the online chatter, along with a debate about whether openly gay pop stars get judged differently.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   NME review →

Music & Awards

Taylor Swift will close the Academy Museum Gala as her Oscar push for “I Knew It, I Knew You” heats up

The Academy Museum announced Thursday that Swift will perform to end its sixth annual gala in Los Angeles on Oct. 17, a night honoring Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo and John Carpenter. The gala is a must-stop for Oscar hopefuls, and Swift is in the original song race for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” her end-credits song for Toy Story 5.

The set list hasn’t been announced, but everyone expects that song to be in it. It became her first No. 1 on U.S. country radio in 13 years and could give her a first Oscar nomination.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Hollywood Reporter →   ·   Deadline →

TV & Streaming

Crazy Rich Asians is coming back as an HBO series, with Constance Wu, Henry Golding and Michelle Yeoh

HBO has ordered eight episodes that pick up after the 2018 film. Wu and Golding return as Rachel and Nick, Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie, and Michelle Yeoh will recur as Nick’s mother, Eleanor. Film co-writer Adele Lim is showrunner, Jon M. Chu executive produces, and production starts next year.

Fans have waited years for a sequel to the box-office hit, which was stuck in development. It’s also one of the first big HBO orders since the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger closed.

BBC →

Bottom of the news
  • John Cena’s Matchbox: The Movie lands on Apple TV with 24% on Rotten Tomatoes.
  • Marvel uses New York Comic Con to announce Zodiac, a 2028 spy series, and screens the first episode of VisionQuest ahead of its Oct. 14 premiere.
  • Grimes releases “Accelerando,” the first single from Psy Opera, her first album in six years.
  • Adéla’s “Nicole Kidman” climbs into the Hot 100’s top 20 while its gospel sample sparks a debate about credit.
  • The Oasis documentary Don’t Look Back in Anger starts streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.
  • Paramount is developing a Cyberpunk 2077 movie.
  • Mike Flanagan’s Carrie series keeps the conversation going on Prime Video, at 85% on Rotten Tomatoes.
  • Bernie Sanders calls David Ellison’s control of CBS, CNN and HBO an “oligarchy” after the Skydance–Warner Bros. deal.

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Thursday, October 8, 2026
item.description:
Thursday · October 8, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Thursday’s conversation: Mia Goth files to end her marriage to Shia LaBeouf, Indian cinema mourns Nana Patekar, Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning limps toward opening weekend as horror takes over, and Kylie Jenner lands her first real acting role on the same day The Kardashians returns.
Celebrity

Mia Goth files for divorce from Shia LaBeouf after nearly 10 years of marriage

The petition, filed Tuesday in Los Angeles County Superior Court, says the couple have been separated since July 2025. Goth, 32, is asking for primary legal and physical custody of their 4-year-old daughter, with visitation for LaBeouf, 40, and wants neither side to receive spousal support. The two met while making Nymphomaniac: Vol. II in 2012 and married in 2016. They announced a split in 2018 but never finalized it, and reunited in 2020.

The timing has people talking: the AP notes that the day before the filing, LaBeouf settled with FKA Twigs for a second time, agreeing to void the NDA from their 2025 settlement so she can speak publicly about her abuse allegations. Representatives for Goth and LaBeouf didn’t immediately comment.

NBC News (AP) →   ·   Los Angeles Times →   ·   FKA Twigs settlement →

In Memoriam

Nana Patekar, one of Indian cinema’s most intense stars, dies at 75

The Hindi and Marathi actor died early Thursday after a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa; doctors said 45 minutes of CPR couldn’t revive him. He became a household name as the gangster Anna in Parinda (1989) and won three National Film Awards, for Parinda, Krantiveer and Agni Sakshi, while showing real range in Khamoshi, the comedy Welcome and Rajneeti. His funeral is Thursday evening in Pune with full state honours.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the tributes, joined by Akshay Kumar, Rajinikanth, Jr NTR and Riteish Deshmukh, who called it “truly the end of an era.” Patekar was also an outspoken activist who co-founded a farmer-welfare foundation, and in 2018 Tanushree Dutta’s harassment allegations against him helped spark India’s #MeToo movement.

BBC →   ·   Indian Express tributes →

Movies

Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning opens Friday to mixed reviews, and Other Mommy is set to win the weekend

Aaron Sorkin writes and directs this “companion piece” to The Social Network, with Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg, Mikey Madison as the Facebook engineer who leaks thousands of internal documents, and Jeremy Allen White as Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz. Critics are split: the BBC gives it two stars and calls Strong’s Zuckerberg “dead-eyed,” Time calls it a brisk, old-school journalism thriller, and Variety’s Guy Lodge says it “already feels behind the curve” but is “diverting enough, clever enough and true enough.”

Variety has it tracking to $7 million to $8 million, far behind the $22 million The Social Network opened to 16 years ago, though it cost a modest $30 million. The weekend should belong to Other Mommy, the James Wan-produced horror film starring Jessica Chastain, which is eyeing $20 million or more from 3,200 theaters on an $18 million budget.

Variety box office →   ·   BBC review →   ·   Trailer →   ·   Other Mommy trailer →

TV & Streaming

Kylie Jenner lands her first scripted lead as The Kardashians returns with Kourtney taking aim at Jennifer Lawrence

Jenner will star in and executive produce Hulu’s Bachelorette Weekend, a murder mystery about a bride found dead in a pool during her bachelorette trip who pieces together what happened while all her closest friends become suspects. Kim Kardashian also executive produces, and Lauren Oliver is adapting an unpublished novel by Flora Collins, according to Deadline. There’s no premiere date yet.

Meanwhile, season 8 of The Kardashians dropped on Hulu overnight, and the premiere has Kourtney unloading on Jennifer Lawrence over last year’s Vanity Fair lie-detector video with Robert Pattinson, in which Lawrence called her “more annoying than ever.” Kourtney’s reply is unprintable here, and she says she told Kris she’d “slap” her.

Time Out →   ·   Daily Mail recap →

Bottom of the news
  • Olivia Rodrigo draws “performative” criticism as women-owned vendors from her Daisy Chain Fields festival say they’re still waiting to be paid; reports suggest it may be resolved.
  • Early 2027 Grammy predictions frame Album of the Year as “Olivia vs. Olivia,” with Rodrigo and Olivia Dean out front.
  • Ramayana releases its English-language trailer for Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s mythological epic.
  • Pitchfork pans Quavo’s Pharrell-produced QRÖMELIFE with a 3.3.
  • Zara Larsson’s “goon face” hiring joke on Las Culturistas sets off an online argument.
  • Justin Timberlake jokes about a paparazzi photo that makes it look like he’s kissing a man’s head.
  • Line of Duty creator Jed Mercurio bids to reboot Doctor Who; the BBC’s shortlist is due Friday.
  • Gaten Matarazzo makes his West End debut as Mark in Rent.

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Wednesday, October 7, 2026
item.description:
Wednesday · October 7, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Wednesday’s conversation: Hollywood says goodbye to Eva Marie Saint, the last star of its Golden Age, Mike Flanagan’s Carrie arrives on Prime Video to strong reviews, the Emmys leave broadcast TV for good, and Miley’s Bass Persuades takes a record-setting chart plunge.
In Memoriam

Eva Marie Saint, the last star of Hollywood’s Golden Age, dies at 102

The actress died Tuesday of natural causes at her home in Los Angeles, surrounded by family, her representative confirmed. She was the oldest living Oscar winner, having won best supporting actress for her very first film role, as Edie Doyle opposite Marlon Brando in Elia Kazan’s On the Waterfront (1954). Five years later she played the cool, dangerous Eve Kendall opposite Cary Grant in Hitchcock’s North by Northwest.

Her career ran from live TV in the late 1940s to an Emmy in 1990 for People Like Us, then Superman Returns, a voice role in The Legend of Korra, and a scripted podcast at 98. Tributes are pouring in, with the Irish Times calling her “one of the immortals.”

BBC →   ·   Hollywood Reporter →   ·   North by Northwest trailer →

TV & Streaming

Mike Flanagan’s Carrie lands on Prime Video, and critics say it’s the most layered version yet

All eight episodes of Flanagan’s Stephen King adaptation are streaming now. Summer H. Howell plays Carrie, with Flanagan regular Samantha Sloyan as her zealot mother, Margaret White, and the story is moved into a present-day high school of viral humiliation, anonymous online bullies and active-shooter drills. It’s told through 911 calls and a documentary-style aftermath, and it’s planned as a trilogy.

Reviews are strong: RogerEbert.com says it’s “not the scariest iteration of Carrie, but it’s the most layered,” and the Seattle Times calls it superb. Some critics knock the added psychic mythology and the finale. King’s first reaction to yet another retelling was “Let the poor girl rest,” though he has since come around.

RogerEbert.com review →   ·   The Verge →   ·   Trailer →

Industry

The Emmys leave broadcast TV: Prime Video takes over the show in a six-year global deal

Starting in September 2027, the Primetime Emmys will stream exclusively on Prime Video through 2032, free and outside the paywall in more than 240 countries and territories. That ends the 31-year rotation among ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox, and makes the Emmys the first of the EGOT shows to go streaming-only (the Oscars don’t move to YouTube until 2029). Variety reports Amazon is paying about $15 million a year for global rights, versus the $8 million to $10 million the networks paid for U.S. rights alone.

Variety →   ·   Hollywood Reporter →

Music

Miley’s Bass Persuades falls from No. 1 to No. 157, the biggest second-week drop ever

A week after debuting at No. 1 with about 61,000 units, her first chart-topper since 2013’s Bangerz, Bass Persuades plunged 156 spots on the new Billboard 200. Variety says it’s the steepest week-two fall for a brand-new album that opened at No. 1 (Bon Jovi and Travis Scott fell further, but with years-old records). Variety points to the lack of a big hit single, since the title track peaked at No. 35. She plays two sold-out Hollywood Bowl shows built around the album on Oct. 16 and 18.

Variety →   ·   Entertainment Weekly →   ·   Listen on Spotify →

Bottom of the news
  • Ted Lasso’s season 4 finale, “Being Alive,” leaves fans emotional and divided; Apple hasn’t confirmed a fifth season.
  • Steven Spielberg will oversee Transformers 8 at Paramount, and Deadline reports Michael Bay is in talks to direct.
  • Skydance’s “Day 1” memo from David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz warns that layoffs are coming after the Warner Bros. merger.
  • Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” debuts at No. 1 on the Hot 100, ending Ella Langley’s record 24-week run with “Choosin’ Texas.”
  • Chet Hanks confronts Eric André at ComplexCon in a viral video before security steps in.
  • Lionel Messi says a tearful goodbye to Argentina, scoring his 126th international goal in a 3–0 win over Benin.
  • Netflix’s live-action Solo Leveling adds Han So Hee, Rain and Lee Sung Min alongside Byeon Woo Seok.
  • Jessica Biel joins Lily-Rose Depp and Bill Pullman in Searchlight’s Playboy Mansion movie Playmates.

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Tuesday, October 6, 2026
item.description:
Tuesday · October 6, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Tuesday’s conversation: the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger is officially done and Hollywood now has a company called Skydance, Andrew Garfield’s Sam Altman lands at the New York Film Festival, Florence Pugh’s East of Eden takes over Netflix, and Hayley Williams fires back at the Department of Homeland Security.
Industry

It’s official: Paramount closes its $110 billion Warner Bros. takeover, and Skydance is born

Paramount Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery this morning, creating a single company called Skydance that trades on the NYSE as SKYD. David Ellison now runs Warner Bros. and Paramount Pictures, HBO Max and Paramount+, CBS, HBO, CNN, DC Studios and franchises from Harry Potter and Game of Thrones to Mission: Impossible. WBD shareholders get about $31.02 a share in cash, and WBD stock stopped trading today. A last-minute petition to halt the deal was denied by Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan.

The bill comes due quickly: the company carries roughly $80 billion in debt and has promised $6 billion in cost savings, which is expected to hit jobs across Hollywood. Under its settlement with a coalition of states, Skydance must release at least 30 films a year or sell its 49% stake in Miramax. CNN chief Mark Thompson stays under a new independent oversight board, and Bari Weiss keeps running CBS News.

NBC News →   ·   BBC →   ·   NPR →

Movies

Artificial premieres at NYFF, and critics call Garfield’s Sam Altman the movie of the moment

Luca Guadagnino’s OpenAI drama, the film Amazon MGM dropped after signing a $50 billion partnership with OpenAI, had its world premiere at the New York Film Festival last night. Andrew Garfield plays Altman, with Yura Borisov as Ilya Sutskever, Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk, Cooper Hoffman as Greg Brockman and Monica Barbaro as Mira Murati, and the story builds to Altman’s firing and rehiring.

Early reactions are glowing, with Next Best Picture calling it possibly “the most urgently relevant film of our time.” On the carpet, Garfield said Altman first struck him as great, honest and transparent, “and then you learn more about a person.” Altman, who hasn’t seen it, told Vanity Fair it “will not be good as an accurate depiction.” Neon opens it in theaters on Christmas Day.

Variety →   ·   NME first reactions →   ·   Trailer →

TV & Streaming

Florence Pugh’s East of Eden is now the No. 1 show on Netflix worldwide

Five days after its Oct. 1 premiere, Zoe Kazan’s seven-part Steinbeck adaptation tops Netflix’s TV charts in the U.S. and globally. Pugh plays Cathy Ames, given far more room than in the 1955 James Dean film directed by Kazan’s grandfather Elia Kazan, opposite Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist as the Trask brothers. The Guardian calls it “brilliant, compelling entertainment.”

Collider →   ·   Trailer →

Music

Hayley Williams answers DHS with a profane Instagram reply after her “F–k ICE” concert moment

During “Ice in My OJ” at a show in Chula Vista, California, the Paramore singer shouted “F–k ICE” and “Free Palestine.” The Department of Homeland Security told Fox News she should “thank them for their service, not belittle their sacrifice.” On Monday, Williams posted that statement to her Instagram Story with a crude, unprintable reply aimed at “Nazi” critics, and it’s been everywhere since.

Billboard →   ·   Rolling Stone →   ·   Listen on Spotify →

Bottom of the news
  • Anne Hathaway apologizes on Fallon for bossing photographers around at the Verity premiere: “mom mode by way of chorus line.”
  • Janhvi Kapoor calls an AI-altered Devara video “deeply violating”; Jr NTR, Chiranjeevi and Vijay Deverakonda condemn it.
  • Simu Liu marries Allison Hsu in a weekend ceremony in France.
  • Tinashe is “cryinggggg” as Popstar debuts at No. 6, her first top-10 album.
  • Victoria Monét’s 22-track Frequency of Love wins Billboard’s weekly new-music poll with 40% of the vote.
  • Netflix’s Unabomber is the most-watched movie on the service worldwide.
  • Meshell Ndegeocello releases Synonym, a duets album with Cynthia Erivo, Chaka Khan and Brandi Carlile.
  • Spider-Man: Brand New Day hits digital today after crossing $2.5 billion (featured yesterday).

item.title: Pop Culture Digest — Monday, October 5, 2026
item.description:
Monday · October 5, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Monday’s conversation: Aaron Sorkin’s Zuckerberg takedown premiered in New York last night, Taylor Swift’s Showgirl is back at No. 1 nine months later, Hollywood wakes up on the eve of the Skydance era, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day joins the $2.5 billion club as it heads to digital tomorrow.
Movies

Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning premieres with a full-villain Zuckerberg — and Meta’s lawyers circling

Aaron Sorkin’s follow-up to The Social Network had its world premiere in New York on Sunday night, four days before it opens in theaters Friday, Oct. 9. The film follows Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) and the Facebook Files, with Jeremy Allen White as Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz and Jeremy Strong as a Mark Zuckerberg that The Hollywood Reporter calls a “full-on villain,” a long way from Jesse Eisenberg’s boyish version.

Sony is leaning all the way in: its ads, running on Instagram and Facebook themselves, tease “Mark Zuckerberg Will Love The Social Reckoning,” then snap back with “Instagram doesn’t fact-check most ads. Why should we?” Sorkin says Meta sent the studio a legal letter. Early reactions praise the film’s bite while knocking its flat, TV-like look. Today also marks five years since Haugen’s Senate testimony.

The Hollywood Reporter →   ·   Deadline premiere photos →   ·   Trailer →

Music

Taylor Swift’s Showgirl vaults 21–1, back at No. 1 nine months later thanks to The Encore

The Life of a Showgirl returns to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 (dated Oct. 10) for a 13th nonconsecutive week on top, powered by the Sept. 25 Encore reissue and its four new songs: “Patient Zero,” “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.” It earned 173,000 equivalent units in the week ending Oct. 1, up 619%, with about 78% coming from streaming. Its last week at No. 1 was back in January.

Elsewhere in the top 10, Tinashe lands her first top-10 album as Popstar debuts at No. 6, and Kenny Chesney’s Silver Sands Marina opens at No. 7. The full chart posts Tuesday.

Billboard →   ·   Listen on Spotify →

Industry

Hollywood’s last day before Skydance: the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger closes Tuesday

Paramount Skydance’s $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery is set to close Tuesday, Oct. 6, after a judge cleared it last week. The combined company, home to Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO, CBS, CNN, MTV, Nickelodeon and more, will be called Skydance and trade on the NYSE as SKYD. Former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz starts today as incoming co-CEO alongside David Ellison.

Deadline reports the TV lineup taking shape: George Cheeks over the combined TV studios and networks, Casey Bloys over HBO Max and Paramount+, and Channing Dungey adding Paramount’s cable networks (MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon, BET) to WBD’s. The official executive structure is expected early this week. It caps a rough weekend for Warner Bros. as a standalone studio, with Digger as its final release and film chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy on their way out.

Movies

Spider-Man: Brand New Day becomes only the third movie ever past $2.5 billion

In its 10th weekend, Sony and Marvel’s Brand New Day crossed $2.5 billion worldwide ($954.5 million domestic, $1.55 billion international), joining only Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. It arrives on digital tomorrow, Oct. 6, with 4K and Blu-ray on Dec. 15, and a re-release is reportedly planned.
